audit.whatIsWrong: The entry states outright that Mel's W is useless here. early: 'his cleaver is a skillshot you can sidestep, but it's not a projectile your Rebuttal wall can eat or reflect, so W does nothing against his main damage here.' whys[2] repeats it: 'W can't eat his non-projectile cleaver.'
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw is a thrown projectile that hits the first enemy struck — the kit flags it projectile, and Mel's Rebuttal reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker. This is the single most important interaction in the matchup and the data asserts the exact opposite of it, telling a Mel player to write off her defining ability against a 975-range cleaver on a 4-second cooldown. The champion-level WKM_LINES entry for Mel already says the opposite.
audit.corrected: Infected Bonesaw is a projectile: Rebuttal both eats it and throws it back at Mundo.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json (W: 'reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker')

audit.whatIsWrong: Goes Where He Pleases is never mentioned anywhere in the matchup, and wants.you[0] tells Mel to open with a Solar Snare root.
audit.why: Mundo's passive resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him. Solar Snare's root is Mel's only hard CC, her gank setup and her disengage — and the first one she lands is eaten. Opening with it is exactly the wrong play; it has to be spent as bait. The cannister he drops restores health and lowers the passive's cooldown when he walks over it, so Radiant Volley's zone denies the pickup.
audit.corrected: Bait the passive with the first root; the second one is the one that holds. Volley the dropped cannister to deny the pickup.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six places credit Mundo with 'Q lifesteal' or 'Q cleaver lifesteal' (early, spikes[0], wants.you[0], whys[0], whys[2], whys[5]).
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw has no healing component. Mundo's sustain is the passive's increased health regeneration, Heart Zapper healing a portion of the damage it stored, and Maximum Dosage. Naming the wrong source sends the Grievous Wounds timing at the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Sustain is passive regen plus Heart Zapper's stored-damage heal, not the cleaver.
sources: champ-data/_kits/drmundo.json (Q has no heal flag; W and R do)

audit.whatIsWrong: late says 'His Q is percent-max-HP, so the tankier he gets the more it hurts you'; spikes[3] and wants.foe[0] repeat the percent-max framing.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw deals damage based on the target's CURRENT health, not max, and not Mundo's. It therefore bites hardest when Mel is full and tapers as she drops — the opposite of the escalating threat the text describes, and it changes when she is allowed to take a cleaver.
audit.corrected: The cleaver scales off your current health: worst at full, weaker as you drop.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns tracked Heart Zapper with no numbers, and wants.you[2] said to trade 'when his Q cleaver is on cooldown'.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw is a flat 4-second cooldown at 975 range — it out-ranges Radiant Volley's 950 and is essentially never down, so 'wait for the cleaver cooldown' is not a real window. Heart Zapper is 17s to 15s, Blunt Force Trauma 9s to 6s, Maximum Dosage a flat 120s.
audit.corrected: Gave the real 4s/975 cleaver, 17s Heart Zapper, and Mel's own 38s Rebuttal, and moved the advice from dodging to reflecting.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.trading and report[3].t both say a wasted Rebuttal leaves Mel bare 'for twenty seconds'.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26 — 38s at the rank this lane is decided at.
audit.corrected: 38 seconds at rank 1, against a cleaver that returns every 4.

audit.why: 16.67% over 6 games is a small sample, but the content layer's level chart (Mundo taking levels 3, 4-5 and first item, skill elsewhere) is a fair reading of a lane Mel cannot kill through. Left as-is.

edits.before: Your one good window is levels 1-2, before Mundo's passive regen and Q cleaver lifesteal are rolling. Land Solar Snare's root and rain Radiant Volley on him while he's stuck — every stack of Overwhelm you bank now matters because you won't get to bank much later. Do NOT trade into a raised Q: his cleaver is a skillshot you can sidestep, but it's not a projectile your Rebuttal wall can eat or reflect, so W does nothing against his main damage here. Dodge the cleaver, root, poke, and respect that his sustain catches up fast.
edits.after: Your one good window is levels 1-2, before Mundo's passive regen and Heart Zapper healing are rolling. Land Solar Snare's root and rain Radiant Volley on him while he's stuck — every stack of Overwhelm you bank now matters because you won't get to bank much later. Infected Bonesaw is a thrown projectile, so Rebuttal eats it and throws it straight back at him: hold W for the cleaver, not for chip. His passive also soaks the first immobilise that lands, so treat your opening root as bait and the second one as the real hold.

edits.before: From level 3 the lane inverts. His E bonus damage and the percent-HP Q mean every cleaver carves a flat chunk of your squishy frame while his passive heals back whatever you poke. You can't out-DPS the drain with a poke kit. At 6 it gets worse — Maximum Dosage is a giant heal-over-time, so even a fully-stacked Golden Eclipse detonate won't execute him; he facetanks your ult and walks. Use your root purely to disengage and survive, not to commit.
edits.after: From level 3 the lane inverts. Blunt Force Trauma's bonus AD and a current-health cleaver every 4 seconds carve your squishy frame while his passive regen heals back whatever you poke. You can't out-DPS the drain with a poke kit. At 6 it gets worse — Maximum Dosage instantly restores a slice of his missing health and keeps regenerating after, so even a fully-stacked Golden Eclipse won't finish him. Use your root purely to disengage and survive, not to commit.

edits.before: This is unwinnable in a straight 1v1 once he itemizes. His Q is percent-max-HP, so the tankier he gets the more it hurts you, and your Overwhelm stores raw magic damage that his huge HP pool and R heal simply absorb. Don't try to fight him — kite with Solar Snare and your move-speed Rebuttal shield purely to stay alive, farm side waves at max range, and let your team peel him while you poke from the back. You will never solo-kill this Mundo; your job is to not die to him.

notes: Highest-value fix in this slice: the entry explicitly told Mel that Rebuttal is dead weight against Infected Bonesaw ('so W does nothing against his main damage here'). The kit flags Mundo's Q as a projectile and Mel's W reflects projectiles at the attacker, so the advice was inverted on the matchup's defining interaction — and it contradicted WKM_LINES.mel[0], which already tells enemies to hold projectiles against her. Same entry also invented 'Q lifesteal' six times (Mundo's Q has no heal) and called the cleaver percent-MAX-health when it is current-health. Because Mundo's passive eats Mel's only hard CC, the whole snare-first gameplan needed reversing. Not fixable through the applier: diff/diffRating/carryRating and every phases[].side and .rating are byte-identical boilerplate shared with 18-315 other matchups, so the applier's exactly-once rule rejects them; the full layer still calls this FAVOURED 4/10 with Mel winning all seven phases of a 16.67% lane.
